name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)
what_you_get: Income support of Rs 6,000 per year, paid in three equal instalments of Rs 2,000 every four months, directly into the farmer family's bank account.
who_can_apply: Land-holding farmer families (husband, wife and minor children) whose names are in State/UT land records

Not eligible: institutional land holders; families where a member holds/held a constitutional post, is/was a Minister, MP, MLA, MLC, Mayor or District Panchayat chairperson; serving or retired government/PSU employees (except Multi Tasking Staff/Class IV/Group D); pensioners getting Rs 10,000 or more a month (except MTS/Class IV/Group D); anyone who paid income tax in the last assessment year; registered practising doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants and architects
The portal notes that farmers who acquired land after 01-02-2019, and cases where more than one family member gets the benefit, are being held back for physical verification
how_to_apply: Register yourself on pmkisan.gov.in under Farmers Corner > New Farmer Registration, or apply through your village Patwari/revenue official or a Common Service Centre (CSC)
The State Nodal Officer verifies your land record, Aadhaar and bank details and uploads approved names
Complete eKYC (mandatory): OTP on the portal, face authentication on the PM-KISAN app, or biometric at a CSC
Check your status any time with Know Your Status (KYS) on pmkisan.gov.in, the PM-KISAN app or the Kisan eMitra chatbot
documents: Bank account number and IFSC (Aadhaar-seeded account)
helpline: Online grievance: https://pmkisan.gov.in/Grievance.aspx. The Ministry's PM-KISAN page tells farmers to call the Kisan Call Centre 1800-180-1551 if an instalment does not come.
source_title: PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi portal (home page: scheme summary, exclusions, latest instalment notice)
as_of: 2026-10-21 (portal states the 23rd instalment was released on 20 June 2026)
latest_update: 23rd instalment released on 20 June 2026 from Tarakeswar, Hooghly, West Bengal (per pmkisan.gov.in). 9,44,65,646 farmers benefited in Apr-Jul 2026-27.
verification_note: Amount, instalments, exclusions and eKYC requirement read on pmkisan.gov.in and its Revised FAQ PDF. The often-quoted helpline numbers 155261 / 011-24300606 / 1800-115-526 were NOT found on any official page I could open, so they are left out.

name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
what_you_get: Crop insurance for notified crops in notified areas. The farmer pays a maximum premium of 2% for Kharif and 1.5% for Rabi foodgrain and oilseed crops, and 5% for commercial and horticultural crops; the Centre and State pay the rest (50:50, or 90:10 in North-Eastern and Himalayan States/UTs).
who_can_apply: All farmers growing notified crops in notified areas, including tenant farmers and sharecroppers (subject to State conditions)
Loanee farmers (with seasonal crop loan/KCC) and non-loanee farmers; enrolment is voluntary for both
Must apply before the season cut-off date notified by the State
how_to_apply: Check that your crop and area are notified for the season on pmfby.gov.in
Apply online at pmfby.gov.in (Farmer Corner), or through your bank branch/PACS, a Common Service Centre, or the insurance company/its agent
Pay your premium share and keep the application number to track status
Report localised or post-harvest losses within 72 hours through the Crop Insurance app, helpline 14447, your bank, CSC or the insurance company
documents: Land record (Khasra/Khatauni/Record of Rights or State equivalent)
Tenants/sharecroppers: tenancy or sharing agreement or State-prescribed certificate
helpline: Krishi Rakshak Portal & Helpline 14447 (toll-free); PMFBY WhatsApp bot +91-70655-14447
source_title: PIB backgrounder: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana - Affordable Crop Insurance for Every Farmer (29 Aug 2026)
additional_sources: https://agriwelfare.gov.in/schemes/pmfby (data: https://agriwelfare.gov.in/api/schemes/pmfby, lastReviewed 2026-10-18) - steps, documents, 72-hour loss reporting, WhatsApp bot number
latest_update: PIB (29 Aug 2026): implemented by 25 States/UTs in Kharif 2026; West Bengal rejoined from Kharif 2026; Bihar to implement from Rabi 2026-27; Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra stopped paying the full farmer premium in 2025.
verification_note: Premium caps and subsidy sharing quoted from the 29 Aug 2026 PIB backgrounder and match the Ministry's scheme page. Cut-off dates and notified crops differ by State and season.

name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) with Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS)
hindi_name: किसान क्रेडिट कार्ड / संशोधित ब्याज अनुदान योजना
what_you_get: Short-term crop loans through KCC at 7% interest, with an extra 3% off for repaying on time, so the effective rate is 4%. PIB (11 Mar 2026) says the MISS crop-loan limit has been raised from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 5 lakh and collateral-free credit from Rs 1.6 lakh to Rs 2 lakh per borrower.
who_can_apply: Individual farmers and joint borrowers who are owner-cultivators
Tenant farmers, oral lessees and sharecroppers
Self Help Groups and Joint Liability Groups of farmers, including tenant farmers and sharecroppers
Fishers, fish farmers and animal husbandry farmers (KCC was extended to fishers and fish farmers in 2018-19)
how_to_apply: Get the one-page KCC application form from your bank's website, pmkisan.gov.in ('Download KCC Form') or the agriculture department
Fill it in with your land record copy and the crops you grow; PM-KISAN beneficiaries' basic details are pre-filled from bank records
Submit at your bank branch (commercial bank, Regional Rural Bank or cooperative bank), or ask a Common Service Centre to fill and send it to the branch
helpline: Kisan Call Centre 1800-180-1551 (listed on the Ministry's KCC page)
source_title: PIB backgrounder: Kisan Credit Card - Fueling Growth in Agriculture (11 Mar 2026)
additional_sources: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2132139&reg=1&lang=1 (28 May 2025: Cabinet continued MISS for 2025-26 with 1.5% subvention to banks; 4% effective rate with 3% Prompt Repayment Incentive)
verification_note: 7%/3%/4% rates and the Rs 5 lakh / Rs 2 lakh limits are quoted from PIB. The same PIB document also says 'Short-term agri-loans up to Rs 3 lakh are available at 7% interest', so it is not fully clear whether the 4% rate covers the whole Rs 5 lakh; show this carefully. I did not find a Cabinet decision continuing MISS for 2026-27. The documents list is from PIB (land records, crop details) plus Aadhaar/bank details from the Ministry's KCC page.

name: PM-KUSUM (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan)
hindi_name: प्रधानमंत्री किसान ऊर्जा सुरक्षा एवं उत्थान महाभियान (पीएम-कुसुम)
what_you_get: Under Component B, individual farmers in off-grid areas can install standalone solar pumps up to 7.5 HP. The Centre gives 30% of the benchmark or tender cost (whichever is lower), the State gives at least 30%, and the farmer pays at most 40%. Component C solarises grid-connected pumps, and Component A supports 500 kW-2 MW solar plants by farmers/groups.
who_can_apply: Individual farmers in off-grid areas (Component B standalone pumps)
Individual farmers, groups of farmers, cooperatives, panchayats, FPOs and Water User Associations (Component A solar plants)
how_to_apply: Apply through your State's PM-KUSUM implementing agency (State nodal agency / DISCOM / agriculture or renewable energy department), which runs the State scheme and tenders
source_title: MNRE: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyaan (PM KUSUM)
verification_note: Subsidy shares are quoted from MNRE. BUT MNRE gives the scheme period as till 31.03.2026. News reports (not official) say MNRE extended timelines only for projects already sanctioned, and that a 'PM-KUSUM 2.0' is being considered. I could not find an official notice either way. Tell farmers to confirm with their State agency before applying. Higher central share for NE/hill States is not shown on the MNRE page I read, so it is left out.

name: Soil Health Card (now 'Soil Health & Fertility' under RKVY)
what_you_get: A printed report for each landholding that tests 12 soil parameters (N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B, pH, EC, organic carbon) and recommends the right fertiliser, bio-fertiliser and organic input doses. The Centre gives Rs 190 per sample to cover collection, testing and card generation.
who_can_apply: All farmers (samples are collected field-by-field by the agriculture department in each sampling round)
how_to_apply: Soil samples are collected by agriculture department staff or trained personnel after the Rabi/Kharif harvest, when no crop is standing
Contact your local agriculture office, soil testing lab or Krishi Vigyan Kendra to get your field included
View and download the card on the Soil Health Card portal (soilhealth.dac.gov.in)
source_title: PIB backgrounder: Soil Health Card - Swasth Dharaa, Khet Haraa (16 Aug 2025)
verification_note: Parameters, Rs 190/sample and the merger into RKVY from 2022-23 are quoted from PIB. The same PIB document says both 'guidance every 2 years' and 'issued once every 3 years', so how often a card is issued is left out. Step 2 (contact local office/KVK) is general advice, not quoted from the source.

name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY)
what_you_get: A pension of Rs 3,000 a month from age 60. The farmer pays Rs 55 to Rs 200 a month depending on joining age, and the Central Government adds an equal amount. If the farmer dies after 60, the spouse gets Rs 1,500 a month as family pension.
who_can_apply: Small and marginal farmers with cultivable land up to 2 hectares in State/UT land records (cut-off date for eligibility: 01.08.2019, per the FAQ)
Age 18 to 40 years at entry (spouses can join separately)

Not eligible: those covered by NPS, ESIC, EPFO or similar statutory schemes; those enrolled in PM-SYM or PM-LVM; institutional land holders; present/former constitutional post holders, ministers, MPs/MLAs/MLCs, mayors, district panchayat chairpersons; serving/retired government and PSU employees (except MTS/Class IV/Group D); income-tax payers in the last assessment year; registered practising doctors, engineers, lawyers, CAs and architects
how_to_apply: Visit your nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) with Aadhaar and bank passbook; enrolment at the CSC is free
PM-KISAN beneficiaries can choose to pay the contribution from the same bank account where PM-KISAN money arrives
source_title: PM-KMY Salient Features (Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, on pmkisan.gov.in)
verification_note: Amounts and eligibility are quoted from the official salient-features and FAQ PDFs. pmkmy.gov.in could not be reached from my network on 2026-10-21. The Ministry's new portal still lists the scheme. The FAQ says names must be in land records as on 01.08.2019; check whether that cut-off has changed.

name: National Agriculture Market (e-NAM)
what_you_get: An online trading platform linking 1,656 mandis in 23 States and 4 UTs (March 2026). Farmers can sell to more buyers through online bidding and get paid straight into their bank account. The e-NAM app gives free price information for 247 commodities.
who_can_apply: Farmers, Farmer Producer Organisations and traders selling through e-NAM-linked mandis
how_to_apply: Register on enam.gov.in (Registration link) or the e-NAM mobile app, or at your e-NAM-linked mandi
Bring your produce to the mandi; it gets a lot ID, quality assaying and online bids
Sale money is paid electronically to your registered bank account
source_title: PIB backgrounder: National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) - Digital Transformation of Agricultural Trade in India (13 Apr 2026)
verification_note: Figures and helpline are from PIB. The helpline also appears on enam.gov.in. The registration-documents page on enam.gov.in is a scanned PDF/JS page I could not read, so documents are left empty. 'Register at your mandi' is general guidance.

name: Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) - micro irrigation
what_you_get: Financial help to install drip or sprinkler irrigation on up to 5 hectares per beneficiary: 55% for small and marginal farmers and 45% for other farmers. Some States add their own top-up subsidy, and the same land can get help again after seven years.
who_can_apply: All farmers (55% for small and marginal, 45% for others), up to 5 hectares per beneficiary
how_to_apply: Apply through your State agriculture/horticulture department or the State's micro-irrigation portal; PDMC is a centrally sponsored scheme run by the States
source_title: PIB backgrounder: Water-Smart Farming with Per Drop More Crop (29 Aug 2026)
verification_note: PDMC was part of PMKSY from 2015-16 to 2021-22. Since 2022-23 it has run under PM-RKVY (per PIB), so it is listed here as PDMC and not as 'PMKSY'. Subsidy rates are quoted from PIB. Application channel and documents differ by State.

name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)
what_you_get: Loans for post-harvest and community farm infrastructure (e.g. warehouses, cold storage) with 3% a year interest subvention on up to Rs 2 crore per project location for up to 7 years. Credit guarantee for loans up to Rs 2 crore is available under CGTMSE, with the fee paid by the Government.
who_can_apply: Farmers
Farmer Producer Organisations and their federations
Primary Agricultural Credit Societies, marketing and multipurpose cooperatives
Self Help Groups and their federations, Joint Liability Groups
Agri-entrepreneurs and start-ups
APMCs, State agencies, cooperative federations, PPP projects
how_to_apply: Register as a beneficiary on agriinfra.dac.gov.in and submit the project/loan application to a participating lending institution (banks, cooperative banks, RRBs, small finance banks, NCDC, NBFCs)
Prepare a project report (DPR templates are on the portal)
helpline: support.agriinfra@gov.in (official support email; helpline numbers on the portal's Contact Us page, Mon-Fri office hours)
source_title: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund portal - Scheme Overview / Who Can Apply / Key Features
verification_note: Interest subvention, credit guarantee, eligible entities and support email are quoted from agriinfra.dac.gov.in. The minimum borrower contribution percentage was seen only on secondary sites, so it is left out.
